• prepayment required via PayPal

• no changes once article is posted

• articles are posted for a minimum of one year but are not permanent

• turnaround time - up to 5 business days (Monday-Friday)


Some topics/links not accepted:

• adult/dating

• male enhancement

• cannabis/marijuana/kratom

• vaping

• peptides

• steroids

• payday loans

• essay writing/related topics

• content directly referencing the University of Iowa/Iowa City

• gambling links that go to sites outside of the U.S.

• content too similar to topics that may be covered by our editorial staff

• articles that appear as reviews questioning whether something is a scam or not

• Bitcoin/Cryptocurrency/Ethereum

• AI*

• some supplements*

• financial/investment•


*There may be some articles related to the topics with an asterisk that we would accept depending on what it is. Our publisher would have to review it.


*Promoted Content Policies*

As the publisher, we reserve the right to review or reject any advertising, including promoted content post, that does not meet our standards of acceptance.

Inappropriate content: We don’t allow ads or destinations that display shocking content or promote hatred, intolerance, discrimination, or violence. We don't allow sexual content in ads and destinations.

Misrepresentation: We don’t allow ads or destinations that deceive users by excluding relevant product information or providing misleading information about products, services, or businesses.

• Examples of misrepresentation: omitting or obscuring billing details such as how, what, and when users will be charged; omitting or obscuring charges associated with financial services such as interest rates, fees, and penalties; failing to display contact information, or physical address where relevant; making offers that aren't actually available; making misleading or unrealistic claims regarding weight loss or financial gain; collecting donations under false pretenses; "phishing" or falsely purporting to be a reputable company in order to get users to part with valuable personal or financial information.

Promoted content posts that violate the above polices may be rejected or removed at any time. Posts that are determined to be misleading or scams after posting will be removed without refund. Once posted, an article removed by the customer will not be refunded.

Subject: [Product Update] Legacy SQL will no longer be available in BigQuery after June 1, 2026
Messages: 1

=== Message 1 ===
From: Google Cloud <CloudPlatform-noreply@google.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 11:41:30 -0800

We are restricting new usage of legacy SQL, your projects are not affected,  
so no action is required.




MY CONSOLE




Hello Oleg,

If you are not familiar with legacy SQL or do not consider it relevant to  
your workflow, please disregard this message.

We're writing to inform you that, after June 1, 2026, the legacy SQL  
dialect in BigQuery will transition to a restricted availability mode in  
your organization/projects. Your organization/projects have not used legacy  
SQL since at least November 1, 2025, so we don't expect them to be affected  
by this change.

What's changing?

After June 1, 2026, any queries written in legacy SQL will fail when run in  
your existing organization/projects or any new organizations. If you have  
queries that use legacy SQL, please follow the migration guide to rewrite  
your queries using GoogleSQL.

What you need to do

Our records show that your organization/projects listed in the attachment  
provided have not executed any legacy SQL queries since at least November  
1, 2025. Based on this finding, no action is required from you, as this  
change will not affect your workloads.

If you believe you need to continue to have access to legacy SQL, please  
refer to Legacy SQL feature availability for more details.

Why are we making this change?

Since 2016, GoogleSQL has been the default, ANSI-compliant standard. We  
recommend using it over legacy SQL for the following operational reasons:


Standardization: It aligns with ANSI SQL standards
Maintenance: It receives all current updates and new system functions
Efficiency: It is a more cost effective option

Please refer to our migration guide for a technical comparison of the two  
dialects.

We're here to help

If you have any questions, please don't hesitate to reach out to Google  
Cloud Support for help.

Thank you for choosing BigQuery.





— The Google Cloud Team

How to Fix It
The address may be misspelled or may not exist. Try one or more of the following:

  *   Send the message again following these steps: In Outlook, open this non-delivery report (NDR) and choose Send Again from the Report ribbon. In Outlook on the web, select this NDR, then select the link "To send this message again, click here." Then delete and retype the entire recipient address. If prompted with an Auto-Complete List suggestion don't select it. After typing the complete address, click Send.
  *   Contact the recipient (by phone, for example) to check that the address exists and is correct.
  *   The recipient may have set up email forwarding to an incorrect address. Ask them to check that any forwarding they've set up is working correctly.
  *   Clear the recipient Auto-Complete List in Outlook or Outlook on the web by following the steps in this article: Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.1.10 in Office 365<https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=532972>, and then send the message again. Retype the entire recipient address before selecting Send.

If the problem continues, forward this message to your email admin. If you're an email admin, refer to the More Info for Email Admins section below.

Was this helpful? Send feedback to Microsoft<https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=525921>.
________________________________

More Info for Email Admins
Status code: 550 5.1.10

This error occurs because the sender sent a message to an email address hosted by Office 365 but the address is incorrect or doesn't exist at the destination domain. The error is reported by the recipient domain's email server, but most often it must be fixed by the person who sent the message. If the steps in the How to Fix It section above don't fix the problem, and you're the email admin for the recipient, try one or more of the following:

The email address exists and is correct - Confirm that the recipient address exists, is correct, and is accepting messages.

Synchronize your directories - If you have a hybrid environment and are using directory synchronization make sure the recipient's email address is synced correctly in both Office 365 and in your on-premises directory.

Errant forwarding rule - Check for forwarding rules that aren't behaving as expected. Forwarding can be set up by an admin via mail flow rules or mailbox forwarding address settings, or by the recipient via the Inbox Rules feature.

Recipient has a valid license - Make sure the recipient has an Office 365 license assigned to them. The recipient's email admin can use the Office 365 admin center to assign a license (Users > Active Users > select the recipient > Assigned License > Edit).

Mail flow settings and MX records are not correct - Misconfigured mail flow or MX record settings can cause this error. Check your Office 365 mail flow settings to make sure your domain and any mail flow connectors are set up correctly. Also, work with your domain registrar to make sure the MX records for your domain are configured correctly.

For more information and additional tips to fix this issue, see Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.1.10 in Office 365<https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=532972>.

The address may be misspelled or may not exist. Try one or more of the following:

If prompted with an Auto-Complete List suggestion don't select it. After typing the complete address, click Send.

More Info for Email Admins
Status code: 550 5.1.10

This error occurs because the sender sent a message to an email address hosted by Office 365 but the address is incorrect or doesn't exist at the destination domain. The error is reported by the recipient domain's email server, but most often it must be fixed by the person who sent the message. If the steps in the How to Fix It section above don't fix the problem, and you're the email admin for the recipient, try one or more of the following:

The email address exists and is correct - Confirm that the recipient address exists, is correct, and is accepting messages.

Synchronize your directories - If you have a hybrid environment and are using directory synchronization make sure the recipient's email address is synced correctly in both Office 365 and in your on-premises directory.

Errant forwarding rule - Check for forwarding rules that aren't behaving as expected. Forwarding can be set up by an admin via mail flow rules or mailbox forwarding address settings, or by the recipient via the Inbox Rules feature.

Recipient has a valid license - Make sure the recipient has an Office 365 license assigned to them. The recipient's email admin can use the Office 365 admin center to assign a license (Users > Active Users > select the recipient > Assigned License > Edit).

Mail flow settings and MX records are not correct - Misconfigured mail flow or MX record settings can cause this error. Check your Office 365 mail flow settings to make sure your domain and any mail flow connectors are set up correctly. Also, work with your domain registrar to make sure the MX records for your domain are configured correctly.

For more information and additional tips to fix this issue, see Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.1.10 in Office 365<https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=532972>.

How to Fix It
The address may be misspelled or may not exist. Try one or more of the following:

  *   Send the message again following these steps: In Outlook, open this non-delivery report (NDR) and choose Send Again from the Report ribbon. In Outlook on the web, select this NDR, then select the link "To send this message again, click here." Then delete and retype the entire recipient address. If prompted with an Auto-Complete List suggestion don't select it. After typing the complete address, click Send.
  *   Contact the recipient (by phone, for example) to check that the address exists and is correct.
  *   The recipient may have set up email forwarding to an incorrect address. Ask them to check that any forwarding they've set up is working correctly.
  *   Clear the recipient Auto-Complete List in Outlook or Outlook on the web by following the steps in this article: Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.1.10 in Office 365<https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=532972>, and then send the message again. More Info for Email Admins
Status code: 550 5.1.10

This error occurs because the sender sent a message to an email address hosted by Office 365 but the address is incorrect or doesn't exist at the destination domain. The error is reported by the recipient domain's email server, but most often it must be fixed by the person who sent the message. If the steps in the How to Fix It section above don't fix the problem, and you're the email admin for the recipient, try one or more of the following:

The email address exists and is correct - Confirm that the recipient address exists, is correct, and is accepting messages.

Synchronize your directories - If you have a hybrid environment and are using directory synchronization make sure the recipient's email address is synced correctly in both Office 365 and in your on-premises directory.

Errant forwarding rule - Check for forwarding rules that aren't behaving as expected. Forwarding can be set up by an admin via mail flow rules or mailbox forwarding address settings, or by the recipient via the Inbox Rules feature.

Recipient has a valid license - Make sure the recipient has an Office 365 license assigned to them. The recipient's email admin can use the Office 365 admin center to assign a license (Users > Active Users > select the recipient > Assigned License > Edit).

Mail flow settings and MX records are not correct - Misconfigured mail flow or MX record settings can cause this error. Check your Office 365 mail flow settings to make sure your domain and any mail flow connectors are set up correctly. Also, work with your domain registrar to make sure the MX records for your domain are configured correctly.

For more information and additional tips to fix this issue, see Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.1.10 in Office 365<https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=532972>.

*Promoted Content Policies*

As the publisher, we reserve the right to review or reject any advertising, including promoted content post, that does not meet our standards of acceptance.

Inappropriate content: We don’t allow ads or destinations that display shocking content or promote hatred, intolerance, discrimination, or violence. We don't allow sexual content in ads and destinations.

Misrepresentation: We don’t allow ads or destinations that deceive users by excluding relevant product information or providing misleading information about products, services, or businesses.

• Examples of misrepresentation: omitting or obscuring billing details such as how, what, and when users will be charged; omitting or obscuring charges associated with financial services such as interest rates, fees, and penalties; failing to display contact information, or physical address where relevant; making offers that aren't actually available; making misleading or unrealistic claims regarding weight loss or financial gain; collecting donations under false pretenses; "phishing" or falsely purporting to be a reputable company in order to get users to part with valuable personal or financial information.

Promoted content posts that violate the above polices may be rejected or removed at any time. Posts that are determined to be misleading or scams after posting will be removed without refund. Once posted, an article removed by the customer will not be refunded.

Thread ID: 19cb011ee164119d
Subject: [Product Update] Legacy SQL will no longer be available in BigQuery after June 1, 2026
Messages: 1

=== Message 1 ===
From: Google Cloud <CloudPlatform-noreply@google.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 11:41:30 -0800

We are restricting new usage of legacy SQL, your projects are not affected,  
so no action is required.




MY CONSOLE




Hello Oleg,

If you are not familiar with legacy SQL or do not consider it relevant to  
your workflow, please disregard this message.

We're writing to inform you that, after June 1, 2026, the legacy SQL  
dialect in BigQuery will transition to a restricted availability mode in  
your organization/projects. Your organization/projects have not used legacy  
SQL since at least November 1, 2025, so we don't expect them to be affected  
by this change.

What's changing?

After June 1, 2026, any queries written in legacy SQL will fail when run in  
your existing organization/projects or any new organizations. If you have  
queries that use legacy SQL, please follow the migration guide to rewrite  
your queries using GoogleSQL.

What you need to do

Our records show that your organization/projects listed in the attachment  
provided have not executed any legacy SQL queries since at least November  
1, 2025. Based on this finding, no action is required from you, as this  
change will not affect your workloads.

If you believe you need to continue to have access to legacy SQL, please  
refer to Legacy SQL feature availability for more details.

Why are we making this change?

Since 2016, GoogleSQL has been the default, ANSI-compliant standard. We  
recommend using it over legacy SQL for the following operational reasons:


Standardization: It aligns with ANSI SQL standards
Maintenance: It receives all current updates and new system functions
Efficiency: It is a more cost effective option

Please refer to our migration guide for a technical comparison of the two  
dialects.

We're here to help

If you have any questions, please don't hesitate to reach out to Google  
Cloud Support for help.

Thank you for choosing BigQuery.





— The Google Cloud Team

SUPPORT

Искусственный интеллект становится ключевым фактором, определяющим финансовую устойчивость и конкурентоспособность бизнеса. Однако внедрение ИИ связано с множеством финансовых вызовов: оценка инвестиционных рисков, расчет ROI, оптимизация затрат и выстраивание прозрачной финансовой стратегии в условиях цифровой трансформации. Именно для решения этих задач Высшая школа экономики разработала уникальную образовательную программу – «ИИ-лидеры: бизнес-лаборатория для руководителей» Для кого эта программа? Программа ориентирована на топ-менеджеров, руководителей отделов и собственников бизнеса, которые хотят раскрыть потенциал искусственного интеллекта в своих компаниях. Это не просто обучение — это настоящая лаборатория, где вы сможете экспериментировать, проверять гипотезы и получать реальные результаты. Что включено в программу? Обучение построено по модульному принципу: каждый из шести модулей длится четыре дня и охватывает ключевые аспекты внедрения ИИ – от стратегии и инфраструктуры до масштабирования успешных решений. Вы изучите не только теорию, но и практические кейсы, а в финале разработаете собственный проект внедрения ИИ в бизнес-процессы. Кто будет преподавать? Преподавателями программы станут эксперты с гигантским индустриальным опытом, из крупных IT-компаний, банков и сферы кибербезопасности, в том числе те, кто прошел путь от разработки алгоритмов искусственного интеллекта до внедрения этой технологии в бизнес. Старт программы: 13 марта. Thread ID: 19c9ff997ad9ba4b
Subject: Ahrefs: Why "best X tool" isn't the prompt you should track
Messages: 1

=== Message 1 ===
From: Andrei from Ahrefs <andrei.tit@ahrefs.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 16:40:59 +0000

Hi o.tsebulevsky@rantsports.com, 
 Last week we launched custom prompts in Brand Radar. Today, I want to show you how to choose the best prompts to monitor your AI visibility (and why most brands are tracking the wrong ones). 
 The problem with broad prompts 
 Let's take a random example: "best CRM tool". Sound logical, right? 
 But here's what we found: 
 - Low commercial intent: most people asking this are browsing, not buying 
- Inconsistent answers: AI platforms rarely give the same result twice 
- Weak signal: you can't tell if visibility here actually drives trials or sales 
 Here's what works better 
 Track groups of high-intent prompts to spot patterns across AI platforms. 
 Instead of "best CRM tool," try: 
 - "Salesforce alternative for small teams" 
- "CRM with the best email automation" 
- "HubSpot vs Pipedrive for agencies" 
 These signal decision-mode, not research-mode. And tracked together, they show whether your brand consistently appears when it matters. 
 Where to find prompts worth tracking 
 Check sources your audience actually uses, like: support tickets, sales calls, PAAs, Reddit/forums, or your own keyword data. 
 [Image "2026-02-13_15-01-59.png?expires=1790857026&amp;signature=ca294cbe2ab1a1acac83fe90f16f28da1acd375199da130646260d6e50bb5622&amp;req=diAhF8t6nIBbXfMW2XS%2FiRS8QVjQT8Ip13vD4abxwFbzj3B56cI%3D%0A"] The goal is to understand what people ask when they're deciding, not just learning. 
Read full article

** 📊 Fact of the Week
------------------------------------------------------------

There is a growing world of independent journalists and a new database that covers it.

It’s called The Independent Journalism Atlas. (https://journalismatlas.com/?utm_source=BuzzStream+Mailer&utm_campaign=ae310b12a8-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_02_26_26&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_0e868c52d2-ae310b12a8-1449626676)

🧐 Why should you care?

There’s virtually no centralized way to discover these journalists, and this localized approach is where a lot of PR is headed.

The Atlas aims to fix that by mapping, standardizing, and connecting this emerging collection of independent creators.

💡 What should you do about it?

Start identifying independent journalists in your clients’ niche communities and build relationships.

Many independent creators are more accessible and collaborative than legacy outlets.


** 🐝 Tip of the Week
------------------------------------------------------------

This week’s tip comes from Joe Hewlett, Senior PR & Talent Executive at Connective3. (https://connective3.com/?utm_source=BuzzStream+Mailer&utm_campaign=ae310b12a8-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_02_26_26&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_0e868c52d2-ae310b12a8-1449626676)


** Digital PR x Interviewing Talent and the strategy behind it
------------------------------------------------------------

When you are interviewing talent around the FIFA World Cup, access alone is not the win. Everyone has access. What matters is how you turn that access into authority.

From my experience interviewing elite athletes and landing coverage in top-tier media, the brands that get real results treat interviews as strategic assets, not just content opportunities.

Here is how brands can actually leverage them:

1. Lead with insight, not hype.

Do not chase generic quotes.

Journalists are looking for a perspective that explains what is happening, not commentary that simply repeats it.

Ask better questions. Pull out insight around performance pressure, leadership, culture, recovery, mindset, or commercial impact. If the talent adds context to the wider narrative, editors are far more likely to use it.

Action: Build interview questions around current storylines and trends, not just the athlete’s performance.

2. Create consistency, not one-off moments.

One interview during a major tournament is noise. A consistent stream of expert-led commentary builds trust.

When journalists know you can deliver thoughtful angles quickly and reliably, they return to you. That repeat coverage compounds over time, strengthening brand positioning.

Action: Map out key tournament moments in advance and plan commentary around each phase.

3. Think SEO from the start

The real value often comes from citation. When commentary adds genuine insight, journalists link back. Those high-authority backlinks drive long-term search visibility.

Action: Provide quotable, data-backed insights that make it easy for journalists to cite and link to your site.

4. Tie the commentary to what is already trending

Relevance increases pickup. Align interviews with breaking player news, tactical shifts, standout performances, or cultural conversations happening around the tournament.

Action: Monitor live news cycles daily and be ready to turn around expert commentary within hours, not days.

5. Measure what actually matters

Coverage is not the end goal. Track branded search growth, referral traffic, keyword visibility, social engagement, and conversion impact. That is how you prove commercial value.

Action: Set success metrics before the campaign launches so you know what to optimise for.

Global events like the World Cup create attention.

Brands that win are the ones that turn that attention into authority, search growth, and measurable business outcomes.

—

My take: I absolutely love this—especially the last takeaway.

Digital PR can be tough to measure, but the best way to have a big impact is to keep the bottom line in mind. Don’t just chase links.

We talk all about measuring digital PR in this post. (https://www.buzzstream.com/blog/digital-pr-metrics/?utm_source=BuzzStream+Mailer&utm_campaign=ae310b12a8-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_02_26_26&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_0e868c52d2-ae310b12a8-1449626676)

** 1. Size of Life
------------------------------------------------------------

🔗 Link (https://neal.fun/size-of-life/?utm_source=BuzzStream+Mailer&utm_campaign=ae310b12a8-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_02_26_26&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_0e868c52d2-ae310b12a8-1449626676)

If you ever need some fun content inspiration, head over to Neal.Fun.

This interactive helps users compare the size of living things as they scroll.

I know that these aren’t always the easiest to pull off from a brand perspective, but AI has made interactive, creative content like this a heck of a lot easier.


** 2. Hidden Ketchup Pocket
------------------------------------------------------------

🔗 Link (https://www.heinz.com/heinzdipper?utm_source=BuzzStream+Mailer&utm_campaign=ae310b12a8-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_02_26_26&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_0e868c52d2-ae310b12a8-1449626676)

Ah, the PR product launch. At this point, I feel like I need to include at least one in every newsletter because they are so creative.

This one from Heinz isn’t necessarily a McDonald’s partnership, but it looks just like it.

Instead, they released them in restaurants and stadiums across the world last year.

Got them some fun coverage, including this write-up in Food & Wine. (https://www.foodandwine.com/heinz-dipper-fry-box-11883538?utm_source=BuzzStream+Mailer&utm_campaign=ae310b12a8-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_02_26_26&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_0e868c52d2-ae310b12a8-1449626676)


** 3. Science Cuts in America
------------------------------------------------------------

🔗 Link (https://www.nature.com/immersive/d41586-026-00088-9/index.html?utm_source=BuzzStream+Mailer&utm_campaign=ae310b12a8-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_02_26_26&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_0e868c52d2-ae310b12a8-1449626676)

Nature published a scrollytelling (yes, again, that’s a real term) story that maps the decline in staffing at the major science agencies in the US.

I think this delivery of information is highly underrated in the digital PR realm, and I still haven’t seen a brand take this approach…Perhaps I shall…


** 4. Distracted Touch Screen
------------------------------------------------------------

🔗 Link (https://www.washington.edu/news/2025/12/16/video-drivers-struggle-to-multitask-when-using-dashboard-touch-screens-study-finds/?utm_source=BuzzStream+Mailer&utm_campaign=ae310b12a8-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_02_26_26&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_0e868c52d2-ae310b12a8-1449626676)

This research on distracted driving was done by the University of Washington.

What struck me was the creative methodology.

They used a driving simulator provided by Toyota Research Institute along with a touchscreen that simulated a car's touchscreen. Then they measured factors such as cognitive load and stress levels.

They presented and published (https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3746059.3747683?utm_source=BuzzStream+Mailer&utm_campaign=ae310b12a8-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_02_26_26&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_0e868c52d2-ae310b12a8-1449626676) their findings, and it’s been cited over 130 times.

This kind of study is not outside the realm of what an agency could do for a brand.

Pricing

Additional Fees:

Content Guidelines

To maintain the quality and SEO structure of our website, all articles must
adhere to the following:

   -

   -

   Minimum 700 words
   -

   Concise paragraphs (preferably 5-6 sentences each)
   -

   At least two images (1 featured + 1 within the body)
   -

      -

   4-5 links per article:
   -

      1 do-follow link for the client - Additional do-follow link(s) to
      your client's website can be added for an additional fee.
      -

      1-2 high-authority reference links
      -

      2 internal links to our site (one must be the first link in the
      article)
      -

      Meta description included
      -

   Prohibited Content


   -

   We do not accept articles containing CBD, adult, or dating-related links.
   -

   We do not offer link insertions into existing content.

Failure to meet these requirements may delay publication. We reserve the
right to reject any article that does not align with our standards or
target audience.
What You Can Expect From Us

   -

   Articles are typically published the same day they are received.
   -

   Official publication timeframe: 24-48 hours (may be longer in some
   cases).
   -

   Expect delays on weekends.
   -

   Articles will be indexed on Google at the time of publication.
   -

   Articles remain live on www.EnosTech.com <https://www.enostech.com> for
   the lifetime of the site (as long as it remains under our control).
   -

   Articles are placed under a standard category and are not labeled as
   sponsored content.
   -

   Opportunity for long-term collaboration.

Other Websites We Work With

you with our other sites, including:

   www.TechLifestyler.com

Payment Terms

   -

   If payment is not received, all links will be removed until payment is
   made.
   -

   Late payments may incur a 10% fee.

Please note: We use internal linking software which automatically adds more
links in your article back to our site.

The address may be misspelled or may not exist. Try one or more of the following:

If prompted with an Auto-Complete List suggestion don't select it. After typing the complete address, click Send.
  *   Contact the recipient (by phone, for example) to check that the address exists and is correct.
  *   The recipient may have set up email forwarding to an incorrect address. Ask them to check that any forwarding they've set up is working correctly.
  *   Clear the recipient Auto-Complete List in Outlook or Outlook on the web by following the steps in this article: Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.1.10 in Office 365<https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=532972>, and then send the message again. More Info for Email Admins
Status code: 550 5.1.10

This error occurs because the sender sent a message to an email address hosted by Office 365 but the address is incorrect or doesn't exist at the destination domain. The error is reported by the recipient domain's email server, but most often it must be fixed by the person who sent the message. If the steps in the How to Fix It section above don't fix the problem, and you're the email admin for the recipient, try one or more of the following:

The email address exists and is correct - Confirm that the recipient address exists, is correct, and is accepting messages.

Synchronize your directories - If you have a hybrid environment and are using directory synchronization make sure the recipient's email address is synced correctly in both Office 365 and in your on-premises directory.

Errant forwarding rule - Check for forwarding rules that aren't behaving as expected. Forwarding can be set up by an admin via mail flow rules or mailbox forwarding address settings, or by the recipient via the Inbox Rules feature.

Recipient has a valid license - Make sure the recipient has an Office 365 license assigned to them. The recipient's email admin can use the Office 365 admin center to assign a license (Users > Active Users > select the recipient > Assigned License > Edit).

Mail flow settings and MX records are not correct - Misconfigured mail flow or MX record settings can cause this error. Check your Office 365 mail flow settings to make sure your domain and any mail flow connectors are set up correctly. Also, work with your domain registrar to make sure the MX records for your domain are configured correctly.

For more information and additional tips to fix this issue, see Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.1.10 in Office 365<https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=532972>.

3. Content Guidelines

 * Restricted Topics: We do not publish articles related to cannabis, dating, or
   sexual issues.
 * We reserve the right to refuse links with excessively high spam scores.
 * Sensitive Topics: gambling or sports betting topic is fine. We only publish a
   neutral article with CBD/follower buying link; however, you may include links
   to these topics within the piece.
 * Article Length: Minimum 500 words.
 * Links: No naked links; please use appropriate anchor text.
 * Images: Up to 3 copyrighted and horizontal images as separate attachments
   (not in the document).
 * No text is allowed in the featured image.
 * Sponsored Label: we use a “SPONSORED” label (see an example:
   https://dailynewshungary.com/fat-freezing-and-body-contouring-the-modern-approach-to-a-sculpted-you/
   [https://dailynewshungary.com/how-to-choose-a-perfect-computer-chair/]).
   Other methods also work.
 * We do not publish articles that are misleading or offer significant financial
   gain. The title should not state that someone can earn thousands of dollars
   daily or similar text. We want to remain credible in the eyes of our readers.

How to Fix It
The address may be misspelled or may not exist. Try one or more of the following:

  *   Send the message again following these steps: In Outlook, open this non-delivery report (NDR) and choose Send Again from the Report ribbon. In Outlook on the web, select this NDR, then select the link "To send this message again, click here." Then delete and retype the entire recipient address. If prompted with an Auto-Complete List suggestion don't select it. After typing the complete address, click Send.
  *   Contact the recipient (by phone, for example) to check that the address exists and is correct.
  *   The recipient may have set up email forwarding to an incorrect address. Ask them to check that any forwarding they've set up is working correctly.
  *   Clear the recipient Auto-Complete List in Outlook or Outlook on the web by following the steps in this article: Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.1.10 in Office 365<https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=532972>, and then send the message again. Retype the entire recipient address before selecting Send.

More Info for Email Admins
Status code: 550 5.1.10

This error occurs because the sender sent a message to an email address hosted by Office 365 but the address is incorrect or doesn't exist at the destination domain. The error is reported by the recipient domain's email server, but most often it must be fixed by the person who sent the message. If the steps in the How to Fix It section above don't fix the problem, and you're the email admin for the recipient, try one or more of the following:

The email address exists and is correct - Confirm that the recipient address exists, is correct, and is accepting messages.

Synchronize your directories - If you have a hybrid environment and are using directory synchronization make sure the recipient's email address is synced correctly in both Office 365 and in your on-premises directory.

Errant forwarding rule - Check for forwarding rules that aren't behaving as expected. Forwarding can be set up by an admin via mail flow rules or mailbox forwarding address settings, or by the recipient via the Inbox Rules feature.

Recipient has a valid license - Make sure the recipient has an Office 365 license assigned to them. The recipient's email admin can use the Office 365 admin center to assign a license (Users > Active Users > select the recipient > Assigned License > Edit).

Mail flow settings and MX records are not correct - Misconfigured mail flow or MX record settings can cause this error. Check your Office 365 mail flow settings to make sure your domain and any mail flow connectors are set up correctly. Also, work with your domain registrar to make sure the MX records for your domain are configured correctly.

For more information and additional tips to fix this issue, see Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.1.10 in Office 365<https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=532972>.

How to Fix It
The address may be misspelled or may not exist. Try one or more of the following:

  *   Send the message again following these steps: In Outlook, open this non-delivery report (NDR) and choose Send Again from the Report ribbon. In Outlook on the web, select this NDR, then select the link "To send this message again, click here." Then delete and retype the entire recipient address. If prompted with an Auto-Complete List suggestion don't select it. After typing the complete address, click Send.
  *   Contact the recipient (by phone, for example) to check that the address exists and is correct.
  *   The recipient may have set up email forwarding to an incorrect address. Ask them to check that any forwarding they've set up is working correctly.
  *   Clear the recipient Auto-Complete List in Outlook or Outlook on the web by following the steps in this article: Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.1.10 in Office 365<https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=532972>, and then send the message again. More Info for Email Admins
Status code: 550 5.1.10

This error occurs because the sender sent a message to an email address hosted by Office 365 but the address is incorrect or doesn't exist at the destination domain. The error is reported by the recipient domain's email server, but most often it must be fixed by the person who sent the message. If the steps in the How to Fix It section above don't fix the problem, and you're the email admin for the recipient, try one or more of the following:

The email address exists and is correct - Confirm that the recipient address exists, is correct, and is accepting messages.

Synchronize your directories - If you have a hybrid environment and are using directory synchronization make sure the recipient's email address is synced correctly in both Office 365 and in your on-premises directory.

Errant forwarding rule - Check for forwarding rules that aren't behaving as expected. Forwarding can be set up by an admin via mail flow rules or mailbox forwarding address settings, or by the recipient via the Inbox Rules feature.

Recipient has a valid license - Make sure the recipient has an Office 365 license assigned to them. The recipient's email admin can use the Office 365 admin center to assign a license (Users > Active Users > select the recipient > Assigned License > Edit).

Mail flow settings and MX records are not correct - Misconfigured mail flow or MX record settings can cause this error. Check your Office 365 mail flow settings to make sure your domain and any mail flow connectors are set up correctly. Also, work with your domain registrar to make sure the MX records for your domain are configured correctly.

For more information and additional tips to fix this issue, see Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.1.10 in Office 365<https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=532972>.

From: Michael Coates <kmcoates@gmail.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 01:25:32 -0800
Subject: Re: Interest in collaborating with your website cleanfleetreport.com

Thank you for your interest in contributing to *Clean Fleet Report.* Our
guidelines for submissions are delivered below. A quick summary for the
most frequently asked questions:

·         Our publication's content is *exclusively automotive*.

·         Sponsored post content must be relevant to the site and contain
information *broadly applicable to the wide readership of the site. *Generally,
we do not publish content that is regional or locally focused as this has
little value to our wide readership.

·         Sponsored posts *need to emulate standard editorial features* and
not be merely promotions for the sponsor.

·         Sponsored links must be relevant to anchor text and are available
on a limited number of posts.

·         Sponsored posts will be edited to AP style.

·         Sponsored posts are permanent and can contain up to two do-follow
links.

·         All sponsored posts will include the introductory phrase—*This
article may contain affiliate links.*

·         The fee for an accepted sponsored post is $200, payable via
PayPal after publication.

·         We try to respond about the acceptability of your proposed post
within 24 hours, and will post it within 48 hours of confirmation of
acceptance.

*Michael Coates*

*Editor & Publisher*

*Clean Fleet Report*



*Sponsored Post Guidelines*

*Clean Fleet Report *is a 20-year-old online publication, one of the
leaders in the field of environmental automotive journalism. Our goal is to
have new content daily, but right now we average new stories every 1-3
days. We have steady readership that averages 20-25,000/month with 35,000
pages served monthly. Approximately 80% of our readership comes from
organic search, which is why we insist that *all content (including
sponsored posts) must be relevant to the site's mission*. That also means
that the readership is regularly refreshed. The search audience is
augmented by a growing number of registered subscribers who receive notices
of new postings, which will include sponsored posts. We welcome sponsored
posts, but must have content aligned with our general subject matter and
editorial style to protect the site's reputation and continue to draw
high-quality traffic.



*Our Basic Criteria*

·         Our focus is on advanced automotive technology and vehicles so
most of our articles will be related to those themes; we cover electric
vehicles, plug-in hybrids, hybrids, a variety of advanced automotive
technology such as autonomous cars, clean diesels, alternative fuel
vehicles and high mileage cars and trucks. We will allow some flexibility
on content with sponsored posts, but wish them to be as relevant to our
readers as possible.

·         Our readers are primarily in the U.S. and Canada, so we prefer
content that's relevant to those markets. Our writing and editing style is
geared to those markets even if the sponsored posts links are directed to
sites in other countries.

·         We aim for a minimum of 400 words to a maximum of 600 per post.
We suggest a maximum of 600 words in a sponsored post for general
readability, although we can make exceptions based on the content.

·         We prefer as many relevant, royalty-free photos or illustrations
as possible to augment the text and keep readers engaged. These should be
submitted along with the article. A typical article needs one lead photo
and two photos to be included in the text. If photos are not included this
can delay publication.

·         Posts will be subject to editing for style and content (we
generally follow U.S. AP style), but the sponsor has the final approval.
Articles should be written in a similar style and tone as the site's
editorial content, even if they have sponsored links.

·         Please identify an author of the article and provide an email for
that author (WordPress requirement). The default, which will be used if you
do not identify an author, is "Guest Contributor." Sponsored posts will not
as a general rule carry staff names as the author. The exception would be
if a sponsored link is inserted into a staff-written story.

·         Do-follow outbound links can be included, but should be kept to a
reasonable number (no more than one per paragraph, for instance).

·         We aim to publish accepted posts within 48 hours. In some
instances we can publish in a shorter timeframe.

·         Sponsored posts will be placed in the lead story location on the
homepage as well as in the Car Knowledge homepage section and will remain
on the home page until bumped by new stories. They will remain indexed and
accessible through our search function and content sections. *Clean Fleet
Report *will promote sponsored posts as we do with all posts—on Facebook,
Twitter, LinkedIn, Tumblr and Pinterest.

·         *Posts will be labeled with "May contain paid affiliate links."
so as not to deceive readers and to comply with ethical SEO practices.*

·         *Posts that are submitted without a listed author (or opt for our
default, "Guest Contributor," or without photos or illustration will be
subject to delay for publication or additional charges. *

·         *Posts will be placed on the cleanfleetreport.com
<http://cleanfleetreport.com> main domain, not a subdomain and included in
our site navigation categories.*

·         *Our site is continually indexed by Google and other search
engines. We maintain a high ranking for many keywords and the majority of
our traffic comes from organic search.*

·         Billing information should be included with submitted article or
link.



*Sponsored Links/Inline Advertising*

·         Sponsored links are also available within most articles (subject
to author/editor approval).

·         We do not support sponsored links to unrelated content

·         We can accommodate display advertising and advertising-based
links (which will be branded as such) for sites independent of a given
article.:

·         *We do not accept advertising for or links to sexually-oriented
sites, gambling or cannabis.*

·         Sponsored links are not subject to promotion, although we will
try to move the story in which they are included to the home page for more
visibility (the home page is our most visited page)..

*Costs*

·         *Payment for a permanent sponsored link alone in an existing
article is $99, to be paid within 24 hours of notification of posting,
either via PayPal (Clean Fleet Report's account is at **kmcoates@gmail.com
<kmcoates@gmail.com>**). *

·         *For a permanent sponsored full post the charge is $200, to be
paid with 24 hours of notification of posting, either via PayPal (Clean
Fleet Report's account is at **kmcoates@gmail.com <kmcoates@gmail.com>**).
We will include a link to a short bio for the author or company on the site
as well as permanent do-follow links within the post. Please send
bio/company information along with the article.*

Thread ID: 19c9ff997ad9ba4b
Subject: Ahrefs: Why "best X tool" isn't the prompt you should track
Messages: 1

=== Message 1 ===
From: Andrei from Ahrefs <andrei.tit@ahrefs.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 16:40:59 +0000

Hi o.tsebulevsky@rantsports.com, 
 Last week we launched custom prompts in Brand Radar. Today, I want to show you how to choose the best prompts to monitor your AI visibility (and why most brands are tracking the wrong ones). 
 The problem with broad prompts 
 Let's take a random example: "best CRM tool". Sound logical, right? 
 But here's what we found: 
 - Low commercial intent: most people asking this are browsing, not buying 
- Inconsistent answers: AI platforms rarely give the same result twice 
- Weak signal: you can't tell if visibility here actually drives trials or sales 
 Here's what works better 
 Track groups of high-intent prompts to spot patterns across AI platforms. 
 Instead of "best CRM tool," try: 
 - "Salesforce alternative for small teams" 
- "CRM with the best email automation" 
- "HubSpot vs Pipedrive for agencies" 
 These signal decision-mode, not research-mode. And tracked together, they show whether your brand consistently appears when it matters. 
 Where to find prompts worth tracking 
 Check sources your audience actually uses, like: support tickets, sales calls, PAAs, Reddit/forums, or your own keyword data. 
 [Image "2026-02-13_15-01-59.png?expires=1790857026&amp;signature=ca294cbe2ab1a1acac83fe90f16f28da1acd375199da130646260d6e50bb5622&amp;req=diAhF8t6nIBbXfMW2XS%2FiRS8QVjQT8Ip13vD4abxwFbzj3B56cI%3D%0A"] The goal is to understand what people ask when they're deciding, not just learning.

** 📊 Fact of the Week
------------------------------------------------------------

There is a growing world of independent journalists and a new database that covers it.

It’s called The Independent Journalism Atlas. (https://journalismatlas.com/?utm_source=BuzzStream+Mailer&utm_campaign=ae310b12a8-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_02_26_26&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_0e868c52d2-ae310b12a8-1449626676)

🧐 Why should you care?

There’s virtually no centralized way to discover these journalists, and this localized approach is where a lot of PR is headed.

The Atlas aims to fix that by mapping, standardizing, and connecting this emerging collection of independent creators.

💡 What should you do about it?

Start identifying independent journalists in your clients’ niche communities and build relationships.

Many independent creators are more accessible and collaborative than legacy outlets.


** 🐝 Tip of the Week
------------------------------------------------------------

This week’s tip comes from Joe Hewlett, Senior PR & Talent Executive at Connective3. (https://connective3.com/?utm_source=BuzzStream+Mailer&utm_campaign=ae310b12a8-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_02_26_26&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_0e868c52d2-ae310b12a8-1449626676)


** Digital PR x Interviewing Talent and the strategy behind it
------------------------------------------------------------

When you are interviewing talent around the FIFA World Cup, access alone is not the win. Everyone has access. What matters is how you turn that access into authority.

From my experience interviewing elite athletes and landing coverage in top-tier media, the brands that get real results treat interviews as strategic assets, not just content opportunities.

Here is how brands can actually leverage them:

1. Lead with insight, not hype.

Do not chase generic quotes.

Journalists are looking for a perspective that explains what is happening, not commentary that simply repeats it.

Ask better questions. Pull out insight around performance pressure, leadership, culture, recovery, mindset, or commercial impact. If the talent adds context to the wider narrative, editors are far more likely to use it.

Action: Build interview questions around current storylines and trends, not just the athlete’s performance.

2. Create consistency, not one-off moments.

One interview during a major tournament is noise. A consistent stream of expert-led commentary builds trust.

When journalists know you can deliver thoughtful angles quickly and reliably, they return to you. That repeat coverage compounds over time, strengthening brand positioning.

Action: Map out key tournament moments in advance and plan commentary around each phase.

3. Think SEO from the start

The real value often comes from citation. When commentary adds genuine insight, journalists link back. Those high-authority backlinks drive long-term search visibility.

Action: Provide quotable, data-backed insights that make it easy for journalists to cite and link to your site.

4. Tie the commentary to what is already trending

Relevance increases pickup. Align interviews with breaking player news, tactical shifts, standout performances, or cultural conversations happening around the tournament.

Action: Monitor live news cycles daily and be ready to turn around expert commentary within hours, not days.

5. Measure what actually matters

Coverage is not the end goal. Track branded search growth, referral traffic, keyword visibility, social engagement, and conversion impact. That is how you prove commercial value.

Action: Set success metrics before the campaign launches so you know what to optimise for.

Global events like the World Cup create attention.

Brands that win are the ones that turn that attention into authority, search growth, and measurable business outcomes.

—

My take: I absolutely love this—especially the last takeaway.

Digital PR can be tough to measure, but the best way to have a big impact is to keep the bottom line in mind. Don’t just chase links.

We talk all about measuring digital PR in this post. (https://www.buzzstream.com/blog/digital-pr-metrics/?utm_source=BuzzStream+Mailer&utm_campaign=ae310b12a8-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_02_26_26&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_0e868c52d2-ae310b12a8-1449626676)

** 2. Hidden Ketchup Pocket
------------------------------------------------------------

🔗 Link (https://www.heinz.com/heinzdipper?utm_source=BuzzStream+Mailer&utm_campaign=ae310b12a8-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_02_26_26&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_0e868c52d2-ae310b12a8-1449626676)

** 3. Science Cuts in America
------------------------------------------------------------

🔗 Link (https://www.nature.com/immersive/d41586-026-00088-9/index.html?utm_source=BuzzStream+Mailer&utm_campaign=ae310b12a8-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_02_26_26&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_0e868c52d2-ae310b12a8-1449626676)

Nature published a scrollytelling (yes, again, that’s a real term) story that maps the decline in staffing at the major science agencies in the US.

I think this delivery of information is highly underrated in the digital PR realm, and I still haven’t seen a brand take this approach…Perhaps I shall…


** 4. Distracted Touch Screen
------------------------------------------------------------

🔗 Link (https://www.washington.edu/news/2025/12/16/video-drivers-struggle-to-multitask-when-using-dashboard-touch-screens-study-finds/?utm_source=BuzzStream+Mailer&utm_campaign=ae310b12a8-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_02_26_26&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_0e868c52d2-ae310b12a8-1449626676)

This research on distracted driving was done by the University of Washington.

What struck me was the creative methodology.

They used a driving simulator provided by Toyota Research Institute along with a touchscreen that simulated a car's touchscreen. Then they measured factors such as cognitive load and stress levels.

They presented and published (https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3746059.3747683?utm_source=BuzzStream+Mailer&utm_campaign=ae310b12a8-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_02_26_26&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_0e868c52d2-ae310b12a8-1449626676) their findings, and it’s been cited over 130 times.

This kind of study is not outside the realm of what an agency could do for a brand.

Build agents that run automatically based on triggers and instructions you define  

Hi Oleg,

Cursor now supports automations for building always-on agents.

Automations run on schedules or are triggered by events from Slack, Linear, GitHub, PagerDuty, and webhooks.

These agents can continuously monitor and improve your codebase by following your instructions and using the tools you've configured.

Try Automations ( http://cursor.com/automations )

We've found two categories of automations to be particularly useful:

* Review and monitoring: Automations can catch and fix everything from style nits and inconsistencies to security vulnerabilities and performance regressions.
* Chores: Automations are great for everyday tasks and knowledge work like triaging bug reports, summarizing code changes, and adding test coverage.

Create automations at cursor.com/automations ( https://cursor.com/automations ), or start from a template ( https://cursor.com/marketplace#automations ).

Read more in our announcement ( https://cursor.com/blog/automations ).

Best,

From: Michael Coates <kmcoates@gmail.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 01:25:32 -0800
Subject: Re: Interest in collaborating with your website cleanfleetreport.com

Thank you for your interest in contributing to *Clean Fleet Report.* Our
guidelines for submissions are delivered below. A quick summary for the
most frequently asked questions:

·         Our publication's content is *exclusively automotive*.

·         Sponsored post content must be relevant to the site and contain
information *broadly applicable to the wide readership of the site. *Generally,
we do not publish content that is regional or locally focused as this has
little value to our wide readership.

·         Sponsored posts *need to emulate standard editorial features* and
not be merely promotions for the sponsor.

·         Sponsored links must be relevant to anchor text and are available
on a limited number of posts.

·         Sponsored posts will be edited to AP style.

·         Sponsored posts are permanent and can contain up to two do-follow
links.

·         All sponsored posts will include the introductory phrase—*This
article may contain affiliate links.*

·         The fee for an accepted sponsored post is $200, payable via
PayPal after publication.

·         We try to respond about the acceptability of your proposed post
within 24 hours, and will post it within 48 hours of confirmation of
acceptance.

*Michael Coates*

*Editor & Publisher*

*Clean Fleet Report*



*Sponsored Post Guidelines*

*Clean Fleet Report *is a 20-year-old online publication, one of the
leaders in the field of environmental automotive journalism. Our goal is to
have new content daily, but right now we average new stories every 1-3
days. We have steady readership that averages 20-25,000/month with 35,000
pages served monthly. Approximately 80% of our readership comes from
organic search, which is why we insist that *all content (including
sponsored posts) must be relevant to the site's mission*. That also means
that the readership is regularly refreshed. The search audience is
augmented by a growing number of registered subscribers who receive notices
of new postings, which will include sponsored posts. We welcome sponsored
posts, but must have content aligned with our general subject matter and
editorial style to protect the site's reputation and continue to draw
high-quality traffic.



*Our Basic Criteria*

·         Our focus is on advanced automotive technology and vehicles so
most of our articles will be related to those themes; we cover electric
vehicles, plug-in hybrids, hybrids, a variety of advanced automotive
technology such as autonomous cars, clean diesels, alternative fuel
vehicles and high mileage cars and trucks. We will allow some flexibility
on content with sponsored posts, but wish them to be as relevant to our
readers as possible.

·         Our readers are primarily in the U.S. and Canada, so we prefer
content that's relevant to those markets. Our writing and editing style is
geared to those markets even if the sponsored posts links are directed to
sites in other countries.

·         We aim for a minimum of 400 words to a maximum of 600 per post.
We suggest a maximum of 600 words in a sponsored post for general
readability, although we can make exceptions based on the content.

·         We prefer as many relevant, royalty-free photos or illustrations
as possible to augment the text and keep readers engaged. These should be
submitted along with the article. A typical article needs one lead photo
and two photos to be included in the text. If photos are not included this
can delay publication.

·         Posts will be subject to editing for style and content (we
generally follow U.S. AP style), but the sponsor has the final approval.
Articles should be written in a similar style and tone as the site's
editorial content, even if they have sponsored links.

·         Please identify an author of the article and provide an email for
that author (WordPress requirement). The default, which will be used if you
do not identify an author, is "Guest Contributor." Sponsored posts will not
as a general rule carry staff names as the author. The exception would be
if a sponsored link is inserted into a staff-written story.

·         Do-follow outbound links can be included, but should be kept to a
reasonable number (no more than one per paragraph, for instance).

·         We aim to publish accepted posts within 48 hours. In some
instances we can publish in a shorter timeframe.

·         Sponsored posts will be placed in the lead story location on the
homepage as well as in the Car Knowledge homepage section and will remain
on the home page until bumped by new stories. They will remain indexed and
accessible through our search function and content sections. *Clean Fleet
Report *will promote sponsored posts as we do with all posts—on Facebook,
Twitter, LinkedIn, Tumblr and Pinterest.

·         *Posts will be labeled with "May contain paid affiliate links."
so as not to deceive readers and to comply with ethical SEO practices.*

·         *Posts that are submitted without a listed author (or opt for our
default, "Guest Contributor," or without photos or illustration will be
subject to delay for publication or additional charges. *

·         *Posts will be placed on the cleanfleetreport.com
<http://cleanfleetreport.com> main domain, not a subdomain and included in
our site navigation categories.*

·         *Our site is continually indexed by Google and other search
engines. We maintain a high ranking for many keywords and the majority of
our traffic comes from organic search.*

·         Billing information should be included with submitted article or
link.



*Sponsored Links/Inline Advertising*

·         Sponsored links are also available within most articles (subject
to author/editor approval).

·         We do not support sponsored links to unrelated content

·         We can accommodate display advertising and advertising-based
links (which will be branded as such) for sites independent of a given
article.:

·         *We do not accept advertising for or links to sexually-oriented
sites, gambling or cannabis.*

·         Sponsored links are not subject to promotion, although we will
try to move the story in which they are included to the home page for more
visibility (the home page is our most visited page)..

*Costs*

·         *Payment for a permanent sponsored link alone in an existing
article is $99, to be paid within 24 hours of notification of posting,
either via PayPal (Clean Fleet Report's account is at **kmcoates@gmail.com
<kmcoates@gmail.com>**). *

·         *For a permanent sponsored full post the charge is $200, to be
paid with 24 hours of notification of posting, either via PayPal (Clean
Fleet Report's account is at **kmcoates@gmail.com <kmcoates@gmail.com>**).
We will include a link to a short bio for the author or company on the site
as well as permanent do-follow links within the post. Please send
bio/company information along with the article.*

** 📊 Fact of the Week
------------------------------------------------------------

There is a growing world of independent journalists and a new database that covers it.

It’s called The Independent Journalism Atlas. (https://journalismatlas.com/?utm_source=BuzzStream+Mailer&utm_campaign=ae310b12a8-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_02_26_26&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_0e868c52d2-ae310b12a8-1449626676)

🧐 Why should you care?

There’s virtually no centralized way to discover these journalists, and this localized approach is where a lot of PR is headed.

The Atlas aims to fix that by mapping, standardizing, and connecting this emerging collection of independent creators.

💡 What should you do about it?

Start identifying independent journalists in your clients’ niche communities and build relationships.

Many independent creators are more accessible and collaborative than legacy outlets.


** 🐝 Tip of the Week
------------------------------------------------------------

This week’s tip comes from Joe Hewlett, Senior PR & Talent Executive at Connective3. (https://connective3.com/?utm_source=BuzzStream+Mailer&utm_campaign=ae310b12a8-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_02_26_26&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_0e868c52d2-ae310b12a8-1449626676)


** Digital PR x Interviewing Talent and the strategy behind it
------------------------------------------------------------

When you are interviewing talent around the FIFA World Cup, access alone is not the win. Everyone has access. What matters is how you turn that access into authority.

From my experience interviewing elite athletes and landing coverage in top-tier media, the brands that get real results treat interviews as strategic assets, not just content opportunities.

Here is how brands can actually leverage them:

1. Lead with insight, not hype.

Do not chase generic quotes.

Journalists are looking for a perspective that explains what is happening, not commentary that simply repeats it.

Ask better questions. Pull out insight around performance pressure, leadership, culture, recovery, mindset, or commercial impact. If the talent adds context to the wider narrative, editors are far more likely to use it.

Action: Build interview questions around current storylines and trends, not just the athlete’s performance.

2. Create consistency, not one-off moments.

One interview during a major tournament is noise. A consistent stream of expert-led commentary builds trust.

When journalists know you can deliver thoughtful angles quickly and reliably, they return to you. That repeat coverage compounds over time, strengthening brand positioning.

Action: Map out key tournament moments in advance and plan commentary around each phase.

3. Think SEO from the start

The real value often comes from citation. When commentary adds genuine insight, journalists link back. Those high-authority backlinks drive long-term search visibility.

Action: Provide quotable, data-backed insights that make it easy for journalists to cite and link to your site.

4. Tie the commentary to what is already trending

Relevance increases pickup. Align interviews with breaking player news, tactical shifts, standout performances, or cultural conversations happening around the tournament.

Action: Monitor live news cycles daily and be ready to turn around expert commentary within hours, not days.

5. Measure what actually matters

Coverage is not the end goal. Track branded search growth, referral traffic, keyword visibility, social engagement, and conversion impact. That is how you prove commercial value.

Action: Set success metrics before the campaign launches so you know what to optimise for.

Global events like the World Cup create attention.

Brands that win are the ones that turn that attention into authority, search growth, and measurable business outcomes.

—

My take: I absolutely love this—especially the last takeaway.

Digital PR can be tough to measure, but the best way to have a big impact is to keep the bottom line in mind. Don’t just chase links.

We talk all about measuring digital PR in this post. (https://www.buzzstream.com/blog/digital-pr-metrics/?utm_source=BuzzStream+Mailer&utm_campaign=ae310b12a8-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_02_26_26&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_0e868c52d2-ae310b12a8-1449626676)

** 3. Science Cuts in America
------------------------------------------------------------

🔗 Link (https://www.nature.com/immersive/d41586-026-00088-9/index.html?utm_source=BuzzStream+Mailer&utm_campaign=ae310b12a8-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_02_26_26&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_0e868c52d2-ae310b12a8-1449626676)

Nature published a scrollytelling (yes, again, that’s a real term) story that maps the decline in staffing at the major science agencies in the US.

I think this delivery of information is highly underrated in the digital PR realm, and I still haven’t seen a brand take this approach…Perhaps I shall…


** 4. Distracted Touch Screen
------------------------------------------------------------

🔗 Link (https://www.washington.edu/news/2025/12/16/video-drivers-struggle-to-multitask-when-using-dashboard-touch-screens-study-finds/?utm_source=BuzzStream+Mailer&utm_campaign=ae310b12a8-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_02_26_26&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_0e868c52d2-ae310b12a8-1449626676)

This research on distracted driving was done by the University of Washington.

What struck me was the creative methodology.

They used a driving simulator provided by Toyota Research Institute along with a touchscreen that simulated a car's touchscreen. Then they measured factors such as cognitive load and stress levels.

They presented and published (https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3746059.3747683?utm_source=BuzzStream+Mailer&utm_campaign=ae310b12a8-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_02_26_26&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_0e868c52d2-ae310b12a8-1449626676) their findings, and it’s been cited over 130 times.

This kind of study is not outside the realm of what an agency could do for a brand.

·        Up to 8,000 characters of text (approximately 1,000 words)

·        Instead of submitting a new piece of content, you may
alternatively request a link in an existing piece of content, subject to
editorial approval and provided the content has not already been sponsored
by another advertiser. The fees are the same as for publishing new content.

*Requirements*

·        All content is subject to editorial review and must be written
well. We may reject content that is overly verbose, filling space to insert
keywords and links with the desired density. Your material must not waste
our readers’ time.

·        If we need to correct typos, misspelling and punctuation, there is
an additional fee of $20. For syntax and more thorough rewriting, there is
an additional $30 fee. We prefer your content is submitted without the need
for our editing.

·        All our sponsored posts require a featured image, so please
provide one that is royalty free and include a link to where you obtained
the image from. Images must be at least 1,000 pixels wide.

·        We will add a 'Guest Post' label to the image (example
<https://www.zambiawatchdog.com/zambias-casino-scene/>) , or if you prefer
'Branded content' or 'In association with [you provide name] but we will
not add any text to the post indicating that it is sponsored. This method
lets our audiences differentiate our editorial content from your promotion.
If your promotion is good, people will of course still read it! We do not
believe that search engines read all text in images and, if they do, that
they will rank the post poorly with the Guest Post label.

*   All articles must please be in English

Please see our guidelines below:



* 500+ word articles - relevant topic to the website niche.

* You can add 1 permanent do follow link to your choice of target URL. Additional do follow link(s) to your client's website can be added for an additional fee - 2-3 authority links are acceptable in the post. 

* We do not add sponsored tags.

* All posts are immediately submitted for indexing by our own custom tool.

* We do not guarantee indexing and we will not be issuing refunds if your article is not indexed.

* Please note, if your article contains any content that breaches our guidelines, our team will be adjusting your content to meet our guidelines and proceeding with publication.

pricing system and guidelines involved, which you can find below:


   - *The article should be tech-related (CBD, Casino, and Crypto posts are
   not accepted)*
   - *Human-written and plagiarism-free (max 5%)*
   - *Contain a max of 2 external links*
   - *Word count should be 1200+*
   - *The price is $150*


Here you can also find our Link insertion guidelines:


   - *The DR of your website should be above 25*
   - *Only relevant text edits will be accepted*
   - *We can provide links only from the blog page*
   - *We do not provide links in the intro or conclusion paragraphs*
   - *We provide links only to tech or SaaS-related pages*
   - *The price for a link insertion is $90*


Please note that both guest posts and links will be permanent and
do-follow, without a sponsored tag.

As a payment method, we prefer to proceed with PayPal, and the turnaround
time (TAT) for both guest posts and link insertions is 2 working days.

Feel free to let me know if you have any questions or need further
information.

We look forward to the opportunity to collaborate with you!

* All posts are immediately submitted for indexing by our own custom tool.

* We do not guarantee indexing and we will not be issuing refunds if your article is not indexed.

* Please note, if your article contains any content that breaches our guidelines, our team will be adjusting your content to meet our guidelines and proceeding with publication.

* We do not guarantee link exclusivity in any articles. Link insertion is a service we offer, and there is a small chance another link may be added into your article. 

* All payments must be made within 24 hours to prevent late fees and ultimately link removal.




Cheers,

How to Fix It
The address may be misspelled or may not exist. Try one or more of the following:

  *   Send the message again following these steps: In Outlook, open this non-delivery report (NDR) and choose Send Again from the Report ribbon. In Outlook on the web, select this NDR, then select the link "To send this message again, click here." Then delete and retype the entire recipient address. If prompted with an Auto-Complete List suggestion don't select it. After typing the complete address, click Send.
  *   Contact the recipient (by phone, for example) to check that the address is correct.
  *   The recipient may have set up email forwarding to an incorrect address. Ask them to check that any forwarding they've set up is working correctly.
  *   Clear the recipient Auto-Complete List in Outlook or Outlook on the web by following the steps in this article: Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.1.1 in Office 365<https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=389363>, and then send the message again. Retype the entire recipient address before selecting Send.

Was this helpful? Send feedback to Microsoft<https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=618497>.

More Info for Email Admins
Status code 554 5.4.14

Typically this error occurs because the recipient email address is incorrect or doesn't exist at the destination domain. This can usually be fixed by the sender. However, sometimes the issue needs to be fixed by the recipient or the recipient's email admin. If the steps in the How to Fix It section above don't fix the problem, and you're the email admin for the recipient, try one or more of the following:

The email address exists and is correct - Confirm that the recipient address exists, is correct, and is accepting messages.

Synchronize your directories - If you have a hybrid environment and are using directory synchronization make sure the recipient's email address is synced correctly in both Office 365 and in your on-premises directory.

Errant forwarding rule - Check for forwarding rules that aren't behaving as expected. A forwarding rule can be configured by an admin via mail flow rules or mailbox forwarding address settings, or by the recipient via the Inbox Rules feature.

Mail flow settings and MX records are not correct - Misconfigured mail flow settings or MX records can cause this error. Check your Office 365 mail flow settings to make sure your domain and any mail flow connectors are set up correctly. Also, work with your domain registrar to make sure the MX records for your domain are configured correctly.

Mail loop detected - This error also indicates that the receiving organization's email settings are misconfigured, creating a mail loop when a message is sent to an address that isn't found in their directory. This usually won't disrupt mail flow for recipients that actually exist, but the recipient's email admin should fix the misconfiguration to reduce the chance of any other mail flow issues. A common cause for this loop is that the recipient's domain is configured as "Internal Relay" when it should be "Authoritative." Another common cause for the loop is that both the sender and recipient are part of the same organization, but the sender's mailbox is hosted by Office 365, while the recipient's mailbox is hosted on-premises, and an outbound connector from Office 365 to the on-premises email servers is missing or misconfigured. To fix this, the recipient's email admin should create a correctly configured outbound connector in Office 365 to route the message to the on-premises mailbox.

For more information and tips to fix this problem, see Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.4.14 in Office 365<https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=397497>.

How to Fix It
The address may be misspelled or may not exist. Try one or more of the following:

  *   Send the message again following these steps: In Outlook, open this non-delivery report (NDR) and choose Send Again from the Report ribbon. In Outlook on the web, select this NDR, then select the link "To send this message again, click here." Then delete and retype the entire recipient address. If prompted with an Auto-Complete List suggestion don't select it. After typing the complete address, click Send.
  *   Contact the recipient (by phone, for example) to check that the address exists and is correct.
  *   The recipient may have set up email forwarding to an incorrect address. Ask them to check that any forwarding they've set up is working correctly.
  *   Clear the recipient Auto-Complete List in Outlook or Outlook on the web by following the steps in this article: Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.1.10 in Office 365<https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=532972>, and then send the message again. Retype the entire recipient address before selecting Send.

If the problem continues, forward this message to your email admin. If you're an email admin, refer to the More Info for Email Admins section below.

Was this helpful? Send feedback to Microsoft<https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=525921>.

More Info for Email Admins
Status code: 550 5.1.10

This error occurs because the sender sent a message to an email address hosted by Office 365 but the address is incorrect or doesn't exist at the destination domain. The error is reported by the recipient domain's email server, but most often it must be fixed by the person who sent the message. If the steps in the How to Fix It section above don't fix the problem, and you're the email admin for the recipient, try one or more of the following:

The email address exists and is correct - Confirm that the recipient address exists, is correct, and is accepting messages.

Synchronize your directories - If you have a hybrid environment and are using directory synchronization make sure the recipient's email address is synced correctly in both Office 365 and in your on-premises directory.

Errant forwarding rule - Check for forwarding rules that aren't behaving as expected. Forwarding can be set up by an admin via mail flow rules or mailbox forwarding address settings, or by the recipient via the Inbox Rules feature.

Recipient has a valid license - Make sure the recipient has an Office 365 license assigned to them. The recipient's email admin can use the Office 365 admin center to assign a license (Users > Active Users > select the recipient > Assigned License > Edit).

Mail flow settings and MX records are not correct - Misconfigured mail flow or MX record settings can cause this error. Check your Office 365 mail flow settings to make sure your domain and any mail flow connectors are set up correctly. Also, work with your domain registrar to make sure the MX records for your domain are configured correctly.

For more information and additional tips to fix this issue, see Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.1.10 in Office 365<https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=532972>.

How to Fix It
The address may be misspelled or may not exist. Try one or more of the following:

  *   Send the message again following these steps: In Outlook, open this non-delivery report (NDR) and choose Send Again from the Report ribbon. In Outlook on the web, select this NDR, then select the link "To send this message again, click here." Then delete and retype the entire recipient address. If prompted with an Auto-Complete List suggestion don't select it. After typing the complete address, click Send.
  *   Contact the recipient (by phone, for example) to check that the address is correct.
  *   The recipient may have set up email forwarding to an incorrect address. Ask them to check that any forwarding they've set up is working correctly.
  *   Clear the recipient Auto-Complete List in Outlook or Outlook on the web by following the steps in this article: Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.1.1 in Office 365<https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=389363>, and then send the message again. Retype the entire recipient address before selecting Send.
